ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-a1.title: Smallest primes
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-a1.body:
The primes above $25$ are $29,31,37,\dots$. The two smallest sum to $29+31=60$. (In the shuttle round this was passed on to A2.)

**Answer: $60$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-a2.title: Count
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-a2.body:
(In the contest $T=60$ was passed on from A1.) We need positive integers below $96$ with digit sum $14$. One-digit numbers cannot reach $14$. For two-digit numbers $10a+b$ with $a+b=14$, $a\le9$: $59,68,77,86,95$, all below $96$. That is $5$ numbers.

**Answer: $5$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-a3.title: Diagonal is the diameter
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-a3.body:
(In the contest $T=5$ came from A2.) $\pi r^2=5\pi$ so $r^2=5$. The largest square has its diagonal equal to the diameter $2r$, so its area is $\frac12(2r)^2=2r^2=10$.

**Answer: $10$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-a4.title: Centres form a rhombus
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-a4.body:
(In the contest $T=10$ came from A3, so the radius is $1$.) The four centres form a rhombus of side $2$ made of two equilateral triangles. Taking the lower-left centre as origin, the centres are at horizontal positions $0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3$ (lower-left, upper-left, lower-right, upper-right), so the rectangle's width is $3+1+1=5$. The height is the vertical separation of the rows of centres, $\sqrt3$, plus $2$ radii: $2+\sqrt3$.

Perimeter $=2(5+2+\sqrt3)=14+2\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $14+2\sqrt3$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-b2.title: Simplify each term
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-b2.body:
(In the contest $T=25$ came from B1.) $\sqrt8=2\sqrt2$; $\sqrt{108}\div\sqrt6=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt2$; $\sqrt6\times\sqrt{75}=\sqrt{450}=15\sqrt2$. The sum is $20\sqrt2$, so $a=20$.

**Answer: $20$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-b3.title: Exterior angles sum to 360
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-b3.body:
(In the contest $T=20$ came from B2.) The three equal exterior angles are $40^\circ$, the four others $55^\circ$. These seven sum to $120+220=340$, so the eighth exterior angle is $360-340=20^\circ$. The largest interior angle goes with the smallest exterior angle: $180-20=160$.

**Answer: $160$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-b4.title: Scale factors
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-b4.body:
(In the contest $T=160$ came from B3.) The large vase has surface area $200$. Volumes are in ratio $108:500=27:125$, so lengths are in ratio $3:5$ and areas in ratio $9:25$. Hence $A=200\times\frac9{25}=72$.

**Answer: $72$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-c1.title: Angle sum and parallels
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-c1.body:
Let $\angle DEA=e$. Then $\angle ABC=e$, $\angle EAB=2e$ and $\angle CDE=2e+40$. Since $AB\parallel DC$, the co-interior angles at $B$ and $C$ give $\angle BCD=180-e$. The angles of the pentagon sum to $540$: $e+e+2e+(2e+40)+(180-e)=540$, so $5e+220=540$, $e=64$ and $\angle BCD=116$.

**Answer: $116^\circ$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-c2.title: Count each
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-c2.body:
(In the contest $T=116$ came from C1.) $A$: cubes below $58$: $1,8,27$, so $A=3$. $B$: triangular numbers below $39$: $1,3,6,10,15,21,28,36$, so $B=8$. $C$: primes below $29$: $2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23$, so $C=9$. Total $20$.

**Answer: $20$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-c4.title: Shoelace or subtraction
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-c4.body:
(In the contest $T=10$ came from C3.) The lines meet where $2x+2=20-x$: $(6,14)$. The shaded region has vertices $(0,0)$, $(20,0)$, $(6,14)$, $(0,2)$.

Area $=$ triangle with vertices $(0,0),(20,0),(6,14)$ $\;(=\frac12\cdot20\cdot14=140)$ plus triangle $(0,0),(6,14),(0,2)$ $\;(=\frac12\cdot2\cdot6=6)$ $=146$.

**Answer: $146$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-d1.title: Do the transformations
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-d1.body:
Reflection in $x+y=5$ sends $(x,y)\to(5-y,5-x)$, so $(1,2)\to(3,4)$: $a=3$, $b=4$. Relative to $(2,2)$ the point is $(1,2)$; an anticlockwise quarter turn sends $(u,v)\to(-v,u)$, giving $(-2,1)$, i.e. $(c,d)=(0,3)$. The sum is $3+4+0+3=10$.

**Answer: $10$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-d2.title: Factor pairs of 100
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-d2.body:
(In the contest $T=10$ came from D1.) $pq=T^2=100$ with $p
e q$ integers. Pairs: $(1,100),(2,50),(4,25),(5,20)$ with differences $99,48,21,15$ (negative pairs give the same differences, and $10\cdot10$ is excluded since the roots are distinct). The least difference is $15$.

**Answer: $15$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-d3.title: Angles at the centre
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-d3.body:
(In the contest $T=15$ came from D2, so $\angle BCD=40^\circ$.) The radii $OB$ and $OD$ are perpendicular to the tangents, so in quadrilateral $OBCD$: $\angle BOD=360-90-90-40=140^\circ$. Since $OE\parallel BC$ and $OB\perp BC$, $\angle BOE=90^\circ$, so $\angle EOD=140-90=50^\circ$. Triangle $OED$ is isosceles ($OE=OD$): $\angle ODE=\frac{180-50}2=65^\circ$. Since $OD\perp DC$, $\angle CDE=90-65=25^\circ$.

**Answer: $25^\circ$**

ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-d4.title: Height and bases
ukmt-stmc-2015-16-final-shuttle-d4.body:
(In the contest $T=25$ came from D3, so $AD=DC=24$.) The height is $24\sin30^\circ=12$. Drop perpendiculars from $D$ and $C$ to $AB$: the left overhang is $24\cos30^\circ=12\sqrt3$ and the right overhang is $12/\tan45^\circ=12$. So $AB=12\sqrt3+24+12=36+12\sqrt3$. Area $=\frac12(24+36+12\sqrt3)\cdot12=6(60+12\sqrt3)=360+72\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $360+72\sqrt3$ cm$^2$**
